title: Invariant-Preserving Graph Traversal and Flow in Python: Complexity, Safety, and Empirical Performance
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: This paper presents a lightweight Python engine for graph traversal and flow that preserves formal invariants while delivering predictable performance. We implement breadth-first search, depth-first search, Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm, topological sorting, and connected-component detection on a generic adjacency-list graph. Formal proofs establish that the topological sort respects acyclicity and that Dijkstra's relaxation maintains the optimal-substructure invariant. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 system with 1 physical core and 2 logical threads shows a mean latency of 33 117.52 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 30 196 ops/s over 30 iterations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261028_170131_start_doing_graph_theory}.
